examples.text: Федя, вообще-то это моя рыба!
examples.trans: Fedya, actually that is my fish!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'husband', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Мой муж помог бывшей и мне наврал!
examples.trans: My husband helped his ex and lied to me!

examples.text: Когда мой муж будет помогать тебе...
examples.trans: Next time my husband is helping you...

examples.text: Это мой муж.
examples.trans: This is my husband.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'former', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Мой муж помог бывшей и мне наврал!
examples.trans: My husband helped his ex and lied to me!

examples.text: Это наш бывший мэр.
examples.trans: This is our former mayor.

examples.text: Он мой бывший начальник.
examples.trans: He's my former boss.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (root 'врать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to lied'.

examples.text: Мой муж помог бывшей и мне наврал!
examples.trans: My husband helped his ex and lied to me!

examples.text: Значит, у вас сумасшедшая ночка была?
examples.trans: So, you two had a crazy little night?
